land.text: the Mapuche lands south of the Biobío: 'Chile finally achieved the occupation and integration of the territories south of the Biobío River in 1884'

successors.note: The Occupation of Araucanía page puts the formal end on 1 January 1883 (Villarrica refounded) and Santa María's 1 June 1883 declaration that the whole Araucanía was subjugated.

land.text: Puelmapu, 'a land comprising part of the Argentine pampa and Patagonia', conquered in the Conquest of the Desert, whose last battle was fought on 18 October 1884

successors.note: The page names the provinces only by modern geography; Neuquén, Río Negro and Chubut are the researcher's reading.

correction.text: Mapuche land south of the Biobío ('Araucanía') with Puelmapu, 'a land comprising part of the Argentine pampa and Patagonia'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria shape exists. The Mapuche page says Puelmapu is 'part of the Argentine pampa and Patagonia' and that Argentina conquered it when Chile occupied Araucanía, without dating its extent in 1810; the three Argentine provinces are the researcher's reading. The Occupation page says 'By 1860, land between the Biobío and Malleco was mostly under Chilean control', which disagrees with the 1862 Angol advance; this dossier takes the Biobío as the northern edge until 1861 and dates the loss of the strip to 1862. Chubut was added by the reviewer (am-08-x, 2026-10-19) so that the Argentine half is the same from 1810 to 1878 as in the 1879-1884 keyframes: the last free group 'surrendered two months later in present Chubut Province' (Conquest page).

correction.text: Mapuche land south of the Malleco river line after the Chilean advance to Angol in 1862; 'Saavedra told Mapuches ... of the plan to fortify the Malleco River line' (1867)

keyframe_review.note: The Angol zone (60 km radius, the researcher's reading of 'the Biobío to the Malleco') passes to Chile in 1862; 'Quilapán attacked the Malleco Line and was repulsed' in 1871, so the line held. The Occupation page gives an area only for the later reductions (about 500,000 ha in nearly 3,000 títulos de merced), no area for the free territory.

correction.text: Gulumapu south of the Malleco; Puelmapu reduced to the south of the Río Negro and the Neuquén (Roca 'reaching Choele Choel in two months', 1879; 'Together, both rivers marked a frontier from the Andes to the Atlantic')

keyframe_review.note: The Conquest page dates the second sweep to 1879 and the Río Negro/Neuquén frontier undated; La Pampa passes to Argentina in the 1878-79 sweeps (Lihué Calel clash, 6 December 1878). Which of Neuquén, Río Negro and Chubut were still held in each year is not on this page; the argentine-confederation dossier dates Neuquén to 1881 and Río Negro and Chubut to 1884.

correction.text: Gulumapu south of the Cautín: 'In March 1881 the Chilean army penetrated from the north to Cautín River'; Puelmapu as before

keyframe_review.note: Temuco was founded in February 1881 and Victoria on 28 March 1881; the Temuco 50 km radius is the researcher's reading of the Cautín line. The Villegas campaign of 1881 on the Argentine side is dated but not located by the Conquest page.

correction.text: Only Puelmapu remains: on 1 June 1883 Santa María declared that 'Today the whole Araucanía is subjugated'; the last Argentine battle was on 18 October 1884

keyframe_review.note: From 1883 the Chilean side is gone (Villarrica refounded 1 January 1883). The Conquest page gives only the 18 October 1884 last battle and the last surrender 'two months later in present Chubut Province', so the two-province Puelmapu (Río Negro and Chubut) holds to 1884 on the researcher's reading; the argentine-confederation dossier dates the loss of Neuquén to the Villegas campaign of 1881.

region.text: Araucanía south of the Biobío and Puelmapu, the independent Mapuche country

ledger.note: 1810: the dossier begins with the independent Mapuche country as Chile's first fifty years of independence leave it alone. Page silent on the Mapuche borders in 1810: the Occupation page says only that in 'Chile's first fifty years of independence (1810–1860)' the government gave Araucanía little priority; the start year is the project's scope, not a founding.

region.text: from the Mulchén-Bureo confluence to the remnants of Angol

ledger.note: December 1861: Chile builds its first fort on Mapuche land. 'Saavedra ordered Pedro Lagos to advance to the Mulchén–Bureo confluence. A fort was built from December 1861 to May 1862.'

region.text: the land between the Biobío and the Malleco, 'the remnants of the town of Angol'

ledger.note: 1862: Chile takes Angol and the Biobío-Malleco strip. 'In 1862 Saavedra advanced with a group of 800 soldiers into the remnants of the town of Angol.' The page also says 'By 1860, land between the Biobío and Malleco was mostly under Chilean control'; the region is the researcher's reading.
1862: the Angol advance ends the first contest; Chile holds the strip from now on.

region.text: the Mapuche country south of the Malleco line, where 'Chilean operations included a scorched-earth campaign in summer 1869'

ledger.note: 1868: Chilean operations resume against the Mapuche south of the Malleco. The page lists '1868–1870: Chilean operations included a scorched-earth campaign in summer 1869, parliaments at Toltén and Ipinco ... and a formal declaration of war in May 1870'.
1871: Quilapán is repulsed at the Malleco line and the fighting stops. 'Quilapán attacked the Malleco Line and was repulsed. Hostilities then ceased for 10 years (1871–1881).'

region.text: the pampa of La Pampa, Río Negro and Neuquén

ledger.note: December 1878: Roca's first sweep clashes with the Mapuche at Lihué Calel. 'On 6 December 1878, elements of the Puán Division ... clashed with a native war party'; the Conquest began 'At the end of 1878'.

region.text: the pampa cleared by Roca's sweeps up to the Río Negro

ledger.note: 1879: Roca's second sweep reaches the Río Negro. 'in 1879 General Roca began the second sweep, reaching Choele Choel in two months'; 'Together, both rivers marked a frontier from the Andes to the Atlantic'. The page does not date the line; La Pampa is the researcher's reading of the land north of it.

region.text: Neuquén: 'Within a year Villegas conquered the Neuquén Province (he reached the Limay River)'

ledger.note: 1881: Villegas conquers Neuquén. The Conquest page: the government 'ordered a campaign during 1881 commanded by Colonel Conrado Villegas'; 'Within a year Villegas conquered the Neuquén Province (he reached the Limay River).' (Reviewer am-08-x, 2026-10-19: confidence raised from 1, the page names the province.)

region.text: the Mapuche country south of the Malleco, the 1881 rising

ledger.note: January 1881: the Mapuche of the Malleco zone rise. 'In January 1881 the Mapuches of the Malleco zone rose against the Chilean occupation'; the large rising followed on 5 November 1881 ('attacks on Lumaco, Puerto Saavedra and Toltén failed').

region.text: the Mapuche country from the Malleco to the Cautín

ledger.note: 1881: Chile takes the Malleco-Cautín country after the January rising. 'In January 1881 the Mapuches of the Malleco zone rose against the Chilean occupation'; 'In March 1881 the Chilean army penetrated from the north to Cautín River'; Victoria was founded on 28 March 1881.

region.text: the Lonquimay valley, Cunco and Curacautín, where forts were founded in the summer of 1882

ledger.note: 1882: Chilean forts in the Andean valleys. 'Expeditions founded forts in the Lonquimay valley, at Cunco and at Curacautín.' Only Lonquimay is in the gazetteer; Cunco and Curacautín are not drawn.

region.text: the rest of the Mapuche country, ending with the refounding of Villarrica

ledger.note: 1 January 1883: Chile refounds Villarrica and the occupation of the Araucanía ends. 'On 1 January 1883, Chile re-founded the old city of Villarrica'; on 1 June 1883 President Santa María declared 'Today the whole Araucanía is subjugated'.

region.text: all of the Mapuche country in Chile

ledger.note: 1883: the contest in Chile ends. 'Today the whole Araucanía is subjugated' (1 June 1883).
18 October 1884: the Conquest of the Desert fights its last battle. 'fighting the last battle on 18 October 1884'; the last rebel group 'surrendered two months later in present Chubut Province'.

region.text: the last free land, Río Negro and Chubut (the argentine-confederation dossier has the same two provinces in 1884)

ledger.note: 1884: the last free Mapuche land passes to Argentina. The Mapuche page: 'Chile finally achieved the occupation and integration of the territories south of the Biobío River in 1884, when the last communities surrendered'; the Conquest page's surrender in Chubut is two months after 18 October 1884.

region.text: the independent Mapuche country, ending when 'the last communities surrendered'

ledger.note: 1884: the last free Mapuche communities surrender. 'Chile finally achieved the occupation and integration of the territories south of the Biobío River in 1884, when the last communities surrendered.'

wars.name: Occupation of Araucanía

zones.text: the Mapuche country between the Biobío and the Villarrica line

wars.outcome: Chilean victory: the Malleco line (1862-1871), then Temuco and Victoria (1881), then Villarrica refounded on 1 January 1883; 'Today the whole Araucanía is subjugated' (1 June 1883).
wars.note: Hostilities 'ceased for 10 years (1871–1881)'; the formal declaration of war was in May 1870; the great rising was November 1881.

wars.name: Conquest of the Desert

zones.text: the pampa and northern Patagonia up to the Río Negro and Neuquén

wars.outcome: Argentine victory: the 'Argentine annexation of Patagonia', the last battle on 18 October 1884.
wars.note: Infobox '1870s – 1884'. The campaign was against several indigenous peoples; the page names the Mapuche leaders Calfucurá (1872 raids) and Namuncurá (1875) only in passing.

wars.name: Kingdom of Araucanía and Patagonia (Orélie-Antoine de Tounens)
wars.outcome: No territorial result: Tounens declared the kingdom 'by two ordinances on November 17, 1860 and November 20, 1860', was 'arrested on January 5, 1862' and 'expelled to France on October 28, 1862'.
wars.note: An unrecognised claim over 'the regions of Araucanía and eastern Patagonia'; it held no ground the pages record, so it is not drawn; claimed capital Perquenco.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is dated on the pages opened; the Biobío (to 1861), the Malleco line (1862-1880), the Cautín line (1881) and the Río Negro-Neuquén line (1879) are approximate river-and-fort frontiers.

notes:
Cliopatria has no Mapuche row (checked data/polities.csv). Slug 'mapuche' is the one that captaincy-general-of-chile.json and republic-of-chile.json already use as counterpart.
Thin pages: none of the pages opened dates the Biobío as the frontier in 1810 or gives the terms of the 1825 Parlamento de Tapihue (the Arauco War page and the Spanish Tapihue page are stubs for this); the 1810 start is the project's scope, not a founding, and the `found` event is confidence 1. A gap-filler should open the Spanish-language 'Guerra de Arauco' or 'Pacificación de la Araucanía' pages.
Puelmapu: included because the Mapuche page names it and says Argentina conquered it; Argentine provinces La Pampa, Neuquén and Río Negro (and Chubut for 1879-1884) are the researcher's reading and the pampas were also held by other peoples (Ranquel, Tehuelche) that the pages do not separate. If the reviewer prefers, drop the Argentine half to a separate dossier 'Puelmapu'.
Orélie-Antoine's Kingdom of Araucanía and Patagonia (17-20 November 1860 to 5 January 1862) held no recorded ground and is a war entry only; if wanted it can be its own dossier (capital Perquenco, claimed).
Capitals: none recorded on the pages opened. Chile's 1852 province of Arauco ('to administer all territories south of the Bio-Bío River') was an administrative claim and is not drawn.
Area: the Occupation page gives no area for the free territory (only about 500,000 ha confined to reductions, nearly 3,000 títulos de merced); the infobox comparison could not be made.
Gazetteer: Cunco, Curacautín and Traiguén are not in places.jsonl (Angol, Temuco, Lonquimay, Villarrica are); the region 'Araucania' is used for the whole Mapuche country south of the Biobío.
